correctness.rationale: For independent area-uniform points in the specified opposite lobes, A_0=1/2 by polar integration and A_q→A_0. The axial quartic gives the exact tip gap: dropping y² from the left and adding it on the right forces x⁴≤x²−q², with the lower axial root attainable at y=0. In the opposite cones the dot product is nonpositive, so a pair at distance <R has both norms <R. At q=0 the missed angular strips on this bounded rescaled domain have width O(ε²); the cone-coordinate integral (1/4)∫_{A,B≥0,A²+B²<2} AB dA dB equals 1/8. This proves the ε⁴/2 coefficient, its O(ε⁶) remainder and conditional TV convergence by normalization of indicator densities. Scaling by q gives x²−y²≥1+q²|(x,y)|⁴, so localized dominated convergence yields 4Φ, including the zero region λ≤2, and TV for λ>2. Integrating horizontal depths gives the claimed triangular-area integral. Near λ=2+δ the depths are O(δ) and transverse coordinates O(√δ). In m=(s+t)/2,d=s−t coordinates the quadratic distance term is m²+d²/2 with unit Jacobian from (s,t); half the integral of its squared positive deficit is πδ³/(3√2). Scaling H± by 1/λ recovers the cone integral for the large-λ tail. The critical limit is for fixed λ; the onset is a subsequent limit, not uniform down to the finite-q tip gap. Bound verification notes and Python verifier were inspected, not executed; the independent reproduction is the exact integrals and localization argument above.
